title: Anterior Drawer Test

positions.as_written: Check that the hamstrings are relaxed by palpating them with your fingers behind the proximal tibia, which is part of the technique rather than an optional refinement.
Compare with the other knee, and note the starting position, because a posteriorly sagged tibia gives a falsely large anterior excursion.
A negative test is weak, much weaker than a negative Lachman, and should not be recorded as excluding the injury.
It should not be used as the basis for a reconstruction decision, and a letter reporting only an anterior drawer has not assessed the ligament adequately.
